draft.title: First-order recurrence relations
card: A recurrence relation gives each term from the term just before it. It needs a starting value, written u0, so the list can begin.
The rule u(n+1) = u(n) + 4 means the next term is the current term plus 4. The rule u(n+1) = 3 × u(n) means the next term is 3 times the current term.
To use it, start with u0 and apply the rule again and again. Each answer becomes the input for the next step.
draft.remember: Start with u0, then apply the rule to each term to get the next one.

a.q: A sequence has u0 = 2 and u(n+1) = 3 × u(n) − 1. What is u2?
a.why: u1 = 3 × 2 − 1 = 5. Then u2 = 3 × 5 − 1 = 14. The answer 5 is only u1, so one step was missed.
a.clue: Find u1 first, then use it to find u2.

b.q: Sam saves for a bike. His savings follow u0 = 30 and u(n+1) = u(n) + 12, where n is the week. How much does he have at the end of week 3?
b.why: u1 = 42, u2 = 54 and u3 = 66. The answer $54 is u2, which stops one step too early.
b.clue: Apply the rule three times, starting from u0.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: u2 = 14 in (a), and u3 = $66 in (b).
